courses.title: Journalism: Introduction to Communication, BA Semester 1

topics.title: Nature and process of communication
topics.summary: Definitions, elements and types of communication.
notes: Elements: source, message, channel, receiver, feedback, noise.
Types: intrapersonal, interpersonal, group, public and mass communication.
The 7 Cs: clear, concise, concrete, correct, coherent, complete, courteous.

topics.title: Communication models
topics.summary: Linear, interactive and transactional models.
notes: Lasswell: who says what, in which channel, to whom, with what effect.
Shannon–Weaver: information source, transmitter, channel (with noise), receiver, destination.
Schramm's model adds a shared field of experience; Osgood–Schramm is circular.
outcomes: Apply Lasswell's model to a news story

topics.title: Functions and theories of mass media
topics.summary: Functions of media and early effects theories.
notes: Functions (Lasswell, Wright): surveillance, correlation, transmission of culture, entertainment.
Hypodermic needle (magic bullet) theory assumed powerful direct effects; two-step flow (Lazarsfeld) found opinion leaders mediate.
Agenda setting (McCombs and Shaw): media tell people what to think about.

topics.title: Indian media landscape
topics.summary: Print, broadcast and digital media in India.
notes: Print is regulated through the Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 (replacing the PRB Act, 1867).
Prasar Bharati runs Doordarshan and All India Radio (Akashvani).
Digital news grows through mobile phones and regional languages.

topics.title: Concept of news and news values
topics.summary: What makes news and the elements of a news story.
notes: News values: timeliness, proximity, prominence, impact, conflict, human interest, novelty.
The 5 Ws and 1 H: who, what, when, where, why, how.
Inverted pyramid: most important facts first.
outcomes: Write a lead with the 5 Ws and 1 H

lesson.hook: A minister falls ill; a farmer in your district finds a 3 kg mango. Which is front-page news, and why?
lesson.example: Lead: "Bengaluru recorded 120 mm of rain on Monday, the city's heaviest single-day October rainfall in a decade, flooding underpasses in five wards."

questions.q: What does the inverted pyramid put first?

topics.title: Sources and interviews
topics.summary: News sources, interviewing and verification.
notes: Sources: primary (eyewitnesses, documents) and secondary; on record, off record, background.
Interview types: news, personality, investigative; prepare, listen, follow up.
Verify facts with at least two independent sources.
outcomes: Conduct and write up an interview

topics.title: Reporting beats
topics.summary: Crime, courts, politics, business, sports and development reporting.
notes: Beat reporters cultivate sources in one area.
Court reporting must avoid contempt and identify victims of sexual offences only as the law permits (they must not be named).
Development journalism reports on social and economic progress.
outcomes: Follow legal limits in crime and court reporting

topics.title: News writing styles
topics.summary: Hard news, features and the structure of stories.
notes: Hard news is timely and factual; features add depth, colour and human interest.
Attribution: say who said it; quotes must be accurate.
Headlines are short, active and accurate.
outcomes: Write hard news and feature stories

courses.title: Journalism: Editing and Media Laws, BA Semester 3

topics.title: Copy editing and headlines
topics.summary: Role of the copy editor, editing symbols and headline writing.
notes: Copy editors check accuracy, clarity, style, grammar and legal risks.
Style books keep usage consistent.
Page layout uses grids, hierarchy and white space.
outcomes: Edit copy for accuracy and style

topics.title: Constitutional framework
topics.summary: Article 19(1)(a) and reasonable restrictions.
notes: Freedom of the press is part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) (Romesh Thappar, 1950).
Article 19(2) allows reasonable restrictions: sovereignty, security, public order, decency, contempt of court, defamation, incitement.
The Press Council of India (Press Council Act, 1978) adjudicates complaints against and by the press.
outcomes: Explain press freedom and its limits

topics.title: Defamation, contempt and other laws
topics.summary: Laws journalists must know.
notes: Defamation is a civil wrong and a crime (BNS section 356); truth for public good and fair comment are defences.
Contempt of Courts Act, 1971; Official Secrets Act, 1923; Right to Information Act, 2005.
Copyright Act, 1957 protects original works; fair dealing allows reporting current events.

topics.title: Journalism ethics
topics.summary: Codes of conduct, privacy and fake news.
notes: PCI Norms of Journalistic Conduct: accuracy, fairness, right of reply, privacy.
Paid news and conflicts of interest undermine credibility.
Fact-checking counters misinformation and deepfakes.

topics.title: Radio journalism
topics.summary: Characteristics of radio and radio formats.
notes: Radio is immediate, portable and reaches non-literate audiences; community radio serves local communities.
Formats: news bulletin, talk, interview, discussion, feature, documentary, phone-in.
Write for the ear: short sentences, simple words, round figures.

topics.title: Television news
topics.summary: TV news production, packages and anchoring.
notes: Package elements: voice-over, sound bites, B-roll, piece to camera.
Production roles: producer, reporter, camera person, editor, anchor.
Script format: two columns (video, audio).

topics.title: Shooting and editing
topics.summary: Shot types, camera movement and editing principles.
notes: Shots: extreme long, long, mid, close-up, extreme close-up.
Movements: pan, tilt, zoom, track, crane.
180-degree rule keeps screen direction consistent.

topics.title: Regulation of broadcasting
topics.summary: Laws and bodies governing broadcasting in India.
notes: Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 and its programme and advertising codes.
TRAI regulates carriage and tariffs; MIB licenses channels.
Self-regulation: News Broadcasting and Digital Standards Authority.

courses.title: Journalism: Advertising and Public Relations, BA Semester 5
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (SEP 2024 (BU scheme to confirm), 2026-27)

topics.title: Advertising concepts
topics.summary: Functions, types and models of advertising.
notes: Types: product, institutional, public service, comparative.
AIDA (attention, interest, desire, action) and DAGMAR (defined goals for measured results).
Advertising agency departments: account services, creative, media, production.

topics.title: Copywriting and media planning
topics.summary: Ad copy, visualisation and media selection.
notes: Copy elements: headline, body copy, slogan, call to action.
Media planning metrics: reach, frequency, GRP, CPM (cost per thousand).
ASCI's code governs truthful and decent advertising.
outcomes: Write ad copy for a product

topics.title: PR principles and tools
topics.summary: Definition, publics and PR tools.
notes: PR is managing communication between an organisation and its publics.
Tools: press releases, press conferences, events, house journals, social media.
Crisis communication: respond quickly, be honest, show concern.

topics.title: Corporate communication and CSR
topics.summary: Reputation management and CSR communication.
notes: Corporate identity, image and reputation.
Internal communication engages employees.
CSR communication must avoid exaggeration (greenwashing).

courses.title: Journalism: Digital and Development Media, BA Semester 6
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (SEP 2024 (BU scheme to confirm), 2026-27)

topics.title: Online news
topics.summary: Characteristics of digital journalism and multimedia storytelling.
notes: Digital news is immediate, interactive, multimedia and hypertextual.
SEO helps stories be found; avoid clickbait.
Mobile journalism (MoJo) uses smartphones to report.
outcomes: Write a story for the web

topics.title: Social media and data journalism
topics.summary: Social media for news and data-driven stories.
notes: Verify user-generated content (reverse image search, metadata, geolocation).
Data journalism: obtain, clean, analyse and visualise data.
IT Rules, 2021 set a code of ethics for digital news publishers.

topics.title: Media for development
topics.summary: Development communication and participatory approaches.
notes: Development communication uses media to promote social change (health, agriculture, education).
Diffusion of innovations (Rogers): innovators, early adopters, early majority, late majority, laggards.
Participatory communication involves communities in planning.

topics.title: Media effects and audiences
topics.summary: Uses and gratifications, cultivation and media literacy.
notes: Uses and gratifications: audiences actively choose media to meet needs.
Cultivation theory (Gerbner): heavy TV viewing shapes perceptions of reality.
Media literacy helps audiences evaluate messages critically.

courses.title: Psychology: Foundations of Psychology, BA Semester 1

topics.title: Psychology as a science
topics.summary: Definition, schools and methods of psychology.
notes: Psychology is the scientific study of behaviour and mental processes.
Schools: structuralism (Wundt, first lab 1879), functionalism (James), psychoanalysis (Freud), behaviourism (Watson, Skinner), humanistic, cognitive.
Methods: experiment, observation, survey, case study, correlational.

topics.title: Nervous system and behaviour
topics.summary: Neurons, the nervous system and the brain.
notes: Neurons transmit signals by action potentials and neurotransmitters across synapses.
CNS: brain and spinal cord; PNS: somatic and autonomic (sympathetic, parasympathetic).
Brain lobes: frontal (planning, movement), parietal (touch), temporal (hearing, memory), occipital (vision).

topics.title: Sensation and perception
topics.summary: Thresholds, attention and perceptual organisation.
notes: Absolute threshold and difference threshold (Weber's law: ΔI ÷ I = k).
Gestalt principles: proximity, similarity, closure, continuity, figure–ground.
Depth cues: binocular (disparity, convergence) and monocular (linear perspective, interposition).

topics.title: States of consciousness
topics.summary: Sleep, dreams and altered states.
notes: Sleep cycles of about 90 minutes: NREM stages and REM (dreaming).
Circadian rhythms follow a roughly 24-hour cycle.
Altered states: hypnosis, meditation, drug-induced.

courses.title: Psychology: Learning, Memory and Cognition, BA Semester 2

topics.title: Classical and operant conditioning
topics.summary: Pavlov's and Skinner's learning principles.
notes: Classical conditioning: a neutral stimulus paired with an unconditioned stimulus comes to elicit a conditioned response.
Operant conditioning: reinforcement increases behaviour; punishment decreases it.
Observational learning (Bandura's Bobo doll study).

lesson.hook: Why does your mouth water when you hear a packet of chips being opened?

questions.a: Increasing a behaviour by removing an unpleasant stimulus.

questions.q: In Pavlov's experiment, what was the conditioned stimulus?

topics.title: Models of memory and forgetting
topics.summary: Atkinson–Shiffrin model, working memory and forgetting.
notes: Sensory memory → short-term memory (about 7 ± 2 items, around 20 seconds) → long-term memory.
Baddeley's working memory: central executive, phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, episodic buffer.
Forgetting: decay, interference (proactive, retroactive), retrieval failure; Ebbinghaus forgetting curve.

topics.title: Problem solving and decision making
topics.summary: Concepts, reasoning, heuristics and biases.
notes: Algorithms guarantee solutions; heuristics are shortcuts.
Biases: availability, representativeness, anchoring, confirmation bias.
Functional fixedness and mental set block problem solving.

topics.title: Theories and measurement of intelligence
topics.summary: Theories of intelligence and IQ.
notes: Spearman's g; Thurstone's primary abilities; Gardner's multiple intelligences; Sternberg's triarchic theory.
IQ = (Mental age ÷ Chronological age) × 100 (ratio IQ); modern tests use deviation IQ (mean 100, SD 15).
Emotional intelligence includes perceiving, using, understanding and managing emotions.

topics.title: Principles and methods
topics.summary: Nature and nurture, stages and research designs.
notes: Development is lifelong, multidirectional and shaped by heredity and environment.
Designs: cross-sectional, longitudinal, sequential.
Critical and sensitive periods.

topics.title: Piaget and Vygotsky
topics.summary: Stages of cognitive development and sociocultural theory.
notes: Piaget: sensorimotor (0–2), preoperational (2–7), concrete operational (7–11), formal operational (11+).
Key concepts: schema, assimilation, accommodation, object permanence, conservation.
Vygotsky: zone of proximal development and scaffolding.

topics.title: Erikson and attachment
topics.summary: Psychosocial stages and attachment styles.
notes: Erikson's eight stages, e.g. trust vs mistrust (infancy), identity vs role confusion (adolescence).
Attachment (Bowlby, Ainsworth's strange situation): secure, avoidant, ambivalent, disorganised.
Parenting styles (Baumrind): authoritative, authoritarian, permissive, neglectful.

topics.title: Later development
topics.summary: Adolescence, adulthood and ageing.
notes: Puberty brings physical and hormonal change; identity formation (Marcia's statuses).
Moral development (Kohlberg): pre-conventional, conventional, post-conventional.
Ageing: crystallised intelligence stays stable; fluid intelligence declines.

topics.title: Attribution and social perception
topics.summary: How we explain behaviour and form impressions.
notes: Fundamental attribution error: overemphasising personality in others' behaviour.
Self-serving bias: credit success to self, failure to circumstances.
Primacy effect in impression formation.

topics.title: Attitudes and persuasion
topics.summary: Attitude formation, change and cognitive dissonance.
notes: Cognitive dissonance (Festinger): inconsistency motivates change in attitudes or behaviour.
Elaboration likelihood model: central route (arguments) vs peripheral route (cues).
Prejudice is an attitude; discrimination is behaviour.

topics.title: Conformity, compliance and obedience
topics.summary: Classic studies of social influence.
notes: Asch: people conform to a group's wrong judgement.
Milgram: about 65% obeyed to the highest shock level.
Compliance techniques: foot-in-the-door, door-in-the-face.

topics.title: Groups and pro-social behaviour
topics.summary: Social facilitation, loafing, groupthink and helping.
notes: Social facilitation improves simple tasks in the presence of others; social loafing reduces individual effort in groups.
Bystander effect: more bystanders, less likelihood of help (diffusion of responsibility).
Group polarisation strengthens initial views.

courses.title: Psychology: Psychopathology, BA Semester 5
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (SEP 2024 (BU scheme to confirm), 2026-27)

topics.title: Defining abnormality and classification
topics.summary: Criteria of abnormality and DSM-5-TR and ICD-11.
notes: Criteria: statistical rarity, deviance, distress, dysfunction, danger.
Classification systems: DSM-5-TR (APA) and ICD-11 (WHO).
Biopsychosocial model: biological, psychological and social causes interact.

topics.title: Anxiety and depression
topics.summary: Symptoms and causes of anxiety and mood disorders.
notes: Anxiety disorders: generalised anxiety, panic, phobias, social anxiety; OCD is classified separately in DSM-5.
Major depressive disorder: depressed mood or loss of interest for at least two weeks with other symptoms.
Bipolar disorder involves manic or hypomanic episodes.
outcomes: Identify symptoms of anxiety and mood disorders

topics.title: Schizophrenia and personality disorders
topics.summary: Psychotic disorders and personality disorders.
notes: Schizophrenia: positive symptoms (delusions, hallucinations) and negative symptoms (flat affect, avolition).
Personality disorders are grouped in clusters A (odd), B (dramatic), C (anxious).
Neurodevelopmental disorders include ADHD and autism spectrum disorder.

topics.title: Mental Healthcare Act, 2017
topics.summary: Rights of persons with mental illness in India.
notes: Every person has a right to access mental healthcare.
Attempted suicide is presumed to be under severe stress and is not to be punished (section 115).
Advance directives and nominated representatives.

courses.title: Psychology: Counselling and Therapies, BA Semester 6
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (SEP 2024 (BU scheme to confirm), 2026-27)

topics.title: Counselling process and skills
topics.summary: Stages and skills of counselling.
notes: Stages: relationship building, assessment, goal setting, intervention, termination and follow-up.
Core conditions (Rogers): empathy, unconditional positive regard, genuineness.
Skills: active listening, paraphrasing, reflection of feeling, summarising.

topics.title: Psychotherapies
topics.summary: Psychodynamic, behavioural, cognitive and humanistic therapies.
notes: Psychoanalysis: free association, dream analysis, transference.
Behaviour therapy: systematic desensitisation, exposure, token economy.
CBT (Beck) and REBT (Ellis) challenge irrational thoughts.

topics.title: Tests and assessment
topics.summary: Psychological testing and test properties.
notes: Good tests are standardised, reliable, valid and normed.
Types: intelligence, personality (MMPI, 16PF), projective (Rorschach, TAT), aptitude.
Ethics: informed consent, confidentiality, competence.

topics.title: Stress and well-being
topics.summary: Stress, coping and positive psychology.
notes: General adaptation syndrome (Selye): alarm, resistance, exhaustion.
Coping: problem-focused and emotion-focused.
Positive psychology (Seligman) studies well-being (PERMA).
